title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
why_read: A rigorous new benchmark testing whether LLMs can correctly generate real cybersecurity tool commands, revealing current models are still quite weak at this precise task.
analysis: KaliBench tests language models on translating natural-language security requests into exact command-line invocations for over 1,600 tools on Kali Linux, a distribution built for penetration testing. The benchmark is notable for using deterministic, verifiable checks rather than vague scoring, and for showing that even strong open models get under 42% exact-command accuracy without hints. The authors also show that targeted fine-tuning with these verifiable rewards can bring an 8-billion-parameter model up to the level of a much larger mixture-of-experts model. This is useful empirical work for anyone evaluating LLMs as security operations assistants, showing real limits and a concrete path to improve them.
